rows.reason: Fixed: 'caustic and cold as ever' and 'How now' are on line 78; the key is drawn from his unkind greeting after acid (A), careful speech (B) and cold (D) are each set aside. Form ok.

Fixed: 'strode over the yielding sand' and 'his feet into the marks Bevis left' are both on line 20 with Bevis correctly the strider; the marks (C) are set aside as a result of softness, not its meaning. Form ok.
Fixed: lines 7 and 8 'handing the cards to Thomas Flanagan' establish the card game, line 9 quoted verbatim; the rubber is the play during which talk stopped, so the pause (C) is set aside. Form ok.

Fixed: 'threw down the cards' (line 23) and 'whose turn it was to deal, gathered them up' (line 24) are verbatim; gathering (D) is set aside as a step before dealing, and giving out is drawn from the next game starting. Form ok.

Fixed: 'seemed much agitated' (line 76), the stake 'not so much' the cause (lines 76-77) now paraphrased correctly, and 'betting under conditions so difficult to their friend' (lines 77-78) lead to unease about fairness. Form ok.

Final sentence 'Line 18 names a trick, so a stitch is a sharp pain from running' presents the key as following from line 18's trick, a non sequitur; it never says the trick is a separate item on the list, so distractor D is not clearly set aside, and 'sharp' and 'in the side' are not drawn from anything. Also 'Line 15 shows the players "running" for the whole game' puts line 14's 'the whole game' on line 15.

Fixed: 'sat up and put his fur in order' is on line 22, scratching follows on lines 22-23, the cotton wool and fire are in lines 15-16 and his draggled state on line 11; grooming gives the tidy state and the mess (C) and a command (A) are set aside. Form ok.

Fixed: 'I am a stranger here' is on line 54, Darzee names Nag on line 53 and the setting is the garden; asking 'Who is Nag?' is now tied to being new to the place, and the sad sense (D) is set aside. Form ok.

Fixed: 'with its wings going' (line 7), pumping 'the sign' (line 8), and 'get sad and start bashing themselves' (line 9) are verbatim; the pumping is shown to signal what comes next, and board/card (A, D) are set aside. Form ok.

Fixed: 'went through the serving hatch into the kitchen' correctly cited as lines 31 and 32; 'through' and 'into the kitchen' show an opening between rooms, and the extinguisher (D) on line 31 is set aside as a different butterfly's spot. Form ok.

Fixed: 'Jo's hot temper mastered her' (line 24) and 'in a passion of grief and anger' (line 25) verbatim; the script draws that the temper took charge of Jo and sets aside the shaking (C) as its result. Form ok.

Fixed: 'sounding the ice' and 'a warm spell had preceded the cold snap' are on line 60, 'see if it's all right' on line 61; the warm spell is used to infer thin ice and testing, and skating by the shore (D) is set aside. Form ok.

Fixed: 'you do not spear them' and 'a noise like a knife going into an apple' are on line 19, 'hand's width' on line 18; the knife-into-apple noise shows driving the point through, and D and C (lifting food) are set aside. Form ok.

Fixed: 'Alan from plot fourteen' (line 25) and 'the allotment' (line 1) verbatim; the numbered plot and the marrow lead to a piece of growing ground, and 'the end of the row' (lines 25-26, D) is set aside. Form ok.

Fixed: 'He looks paler than his wont' is on line 11; 'paler than' is now shown to compare today's look with his usual one, and line 15's pictures support the crowd knowing his normal face; reason and refusal set aside. Form ok.

Fixed: line 17 'But, in spite of these signs of approval', line 18 'in silence and with sullen looks', line 19 'an ironical sort of greeting' all verbatim; the script shows 'sullen' adds ill feeling beyond silence, setting aside C. Form ok.

Fixed: 'what landed on' (line 17), 'the slow heavy ones' and 'the ones that hovered' (line 18), 'before they settled' (lines 18-19) verbatim; 'before' shows staying in the air first, setting aside landing straight away (C). Form ok.
